articles.title_zh: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'
facts_zh:
Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'
- Published
Donald Trump has said "Iran militarily is effectively over", and said that there is "positive momentum" behind negotiations to end the Middle East conflict.
"We're just keeping it the status quo," the US president said on Monday.

"And we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours."
Addressing reporters from the White House press briefing room, Trump said that renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" but that the US was "locked and loaded" should the circumstances change.

facts_zh:
Qantas to outsource 850 local jobs with most roles moving to India
- Published
Qantas will outsource 850 local corporate jobs to consulting giant Accenture with most roles moving to India as the airline fast-tracks AI investment.
In an internal email to staff on Tuesday, the Australian company's CEO Vanessa Hudson said "this is hard news for some and I'm sorry for the uncertainty it brings".

The job cuts will begin mid-2027, she said, and start with finance, procurement, people and marketing roles shifting "mostly" to teams in India and "some in Australia" as the firm seeks to modernise its IT systems.

Trial date of alleged Charlie Kirk killer set for June 2028
- Published
The trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk, will start in June 2028, a judge has ordered.
Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and six other charges in connection with the September 2025 killing of Kirk, 31, who was shot while he spoke at a Utah college campus.
Utah County judge Tony Graf Jr on Monday told the court that jury selection would begin on 21 June, 2028.

A Massachusetts judge has denied motions to dismiss the murder case of Lindsay Clancy, the US woman accused of murdering her three children, according to local US media.

The ruling clears the way for prosecutors to pursue the case.

All those killed and injured were workers at the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga, one of the country's leading steel producers, authorities said.
Footage from the scene showed a large fire inside the facility and a towering column of smoke rising into the air.

- Published
France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month.
Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions.
Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.

articles.title_original: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
articles.title_zh: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
facts_zh:
Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
- Published
A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow, and his parents and sister at their home, died in hospital early on Monday, Polish police have said.
The 24-year-old, who has been named as Michal Oksinski by local media, was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday, police said.
Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.

all_titles.en: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say

articles.title_zh: Deadly floods hit Iraq as thunderstorms sweep across region
facts_zh: Violent storms lash northern Iraq and parts of Iran, while Portugal faces strong winds and Japan braces for further snowfall Deadly flash floods hit northern Iraq on Saturday as severe thunderstorms swept across the region, including in neighbouring Iran.
The city of Erbil, in Iraq, was particularly badly hit, with extensive damage to homes and businesses.
Streets were inundated as torrential rain fell over a short period.

articles.title_original: Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
articles.title_zh: Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
facts_zh:
Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
- Published
Three children and one woman were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in central Gaza following heavy rain, the Hamas-run health ministry says.
Five injured people were also reportedly rescued after the incident on Sunday night at a camp for displaced families south of Deir al-Balah.
Videos showed men using phone torches to search for survivors beneath boulders, sand and collapsed tents.

all_titles.en: Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
